adversarialFinding.summary: Postal DomainDNSError is a domain-level webhook carrying SPF/DKIM/MX/return-path status and no message/tag. The prior normalizer required message identity for every mapped event, so authentic DNS failures were quarantined as MALFORMED. At the same time, postal-effect-adapter treated DNS_ERROR as message submission proof, which is the wrong semantic boundary.
adversarialFinding.officialEvidence: Postal webhook documentation defines DomainDNSError as a domain DNS monitoring event with domain, dns_checked_at, SPF/DKIM/MX/return-path fields and no message object; MessageBounced and message status events are separate message lifecycle events.

implemented: DomainDNSError now has a dedicated authenticated domain-level normalization path.
Authenticated DNS events persist normalized domain plus SPF/DKIM/MX/return-path statuses and digests of error text without retaining raw error content.
DomainDNSError becomes eligibleForSenderEvidence=true only when SHA-256 authenticated and structurally valid.
DomainDNSError remains eligibleForReconciliation=false and carries no execution tag or Postal message id.
DNS_ERROR and DOMAINDNSERROR were removed from message SUBMISSION_PROOF_STATUSES and NEGATIVE_DELIVERY_STATUSES.
Webhook route exposes senderEvidenceAvailable separately from reconciliationRequired while retaining businessEffectAuthority=NONE.
Hostile tests cover authenticated and unauthenticated DNS events, no secret leakage, route semantics, and separation from message reconciliation.
Mutation protection now fails if DNS sender evidence is reintroduced as message submission/delivery proof.
